status_note: REFERENCED (2026-09-01) — shipped to the public catalog. Multi-dimensional skill program on the pull-up + handstand-adjacent drill libraries. Tier A (prep) → Tier C (first strict ring muscle-up). Not yet REVIEWED: no domain-specialist audit, so `reviewed_by` / `review_evidence[]` are deliberately absent.

goals.primary_intent: Get your first strict ring muscle-up — no kip, no swing, from a dead hang, through the transition, to a locked-out ring support. Sub-capabilities (false-grip pull, transition control, ring dip strength, straight-arm shoulder integrity, hollow shape) train as independent state variables. Weekly plan targets the weakest measured capability first (Henry 1968; Proteau 1992).

arc.block_1_this_program: 10-16 weeks. Tier A builds false-grip tolerance + first ring dip base for users who have the prerequisite pull-up and dip counts. Tier B builds transition mechanics (seated-band + low-ring). Tier C attempts the first strict rep.
arc.block_2_expected: 8-12 weeks. Volume: 1 → 3 unbroken strict ring muscle-ups. Turnover speed + potentially the bar muscle-up variant.
arc.note: No cohort ETA. The strict ring muscle-up is a low-frequency skill for even experienced calisthenics athletes — the transition point is the technical bottleneck, and Roig 2011 shoulder-loading analog and Youdas 2010 grip / EMG work inform the drill order rather than promising a timeline.

principles.rule: 3-5 strict pull-ups AND 3-5 ring dips are the intake floor. Below either, the program routes the user to the pre-req program.
principles.detail: Engineering choice + coach consensus (Sommer 2008 commentary; Low 2016 coach writing) — not RCT-derived. Rationale: the muscle-up is a strength move stitched together from three sub-lifts. Without the constituent strength, the transition drills groove a compensation (kip / swing) that reinforces itself. If a user lands here without the prerequisite, the manifest routes them to First Strict Pull-Up or the ring-dip prep in this program.

principles.rule: False-grip tolerance is trained before any transition attempt
principles.detail: The false grip (wrist above the rings) is the mechanical enabler of the transition — it removes the need to re-grip mid-lift. Vidal-Rovira 2024 (small-sample) documents higher forearm activation in false-grip vs standard hang. Untrained wrists lose the grip in the transition and the athlete drops out. Building false-grip hang time + false-grip ring row + false-grip pull-up is the Tier A / B primary.

principles.rule: Every drill in Tier B and C targets the transition — not the pull, not the dip
principles.detail: Pull and dip strength are prerequisites, not the training target here. The seated-band transition, the low-ring transition, and the negative-from-support-position drills isolate the turnover mechanic (elbows travelling from behind you to in front of you at chest height). This is where the strict muscle-up is won or lost.

principles.rule: Every drill card renders an external-focus cue by default (Wulf 1998, 2013)
principles.detail: External focus outperforms internal for complex motor skill acquisition. Cues target the ring path (pull rings to sternum, drive rings down past hips), not the muscles.

principles.rule: Video review is a button, not a schedule (Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002)
principles.detail: The transition is a visual-mechanical skill. Video KP is the highest-value feedback for it, but Potdevin 2018 (n=18 gymnastics children, 8 weeks) found KP after ~5 reps outperformed KP after every rep. Self-selected surfaces after every set as optional.

principles.rule: Any shoulder pain during a hang, transition, or support hold ends the session — no working through it
principles.detail: Support position on rings loads the long head of biceps + supraspinatus at end-range. Sadowski 2021 (straight-arm press to handstand: 3× BW shoulder moment) is the analog — support lockout on rings sees similar peak moments. Pain-through reinforces the compensation.

principles.rule: This is a strict-muscle-up program. Kipping muscle-ups are a different skill and are not the goal here.
principles.detail: Kipping muscle-ups train a different neural pattern (hip drive → false-grip re-catch is kinetic-chain-dependent). Users who want kipping muscle-ups should train them separately. Deliberate segregation avoids fouling the strict pattern (Henry 1968 specificity: two different tasks).

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. Muscle-up work benefits from spacing — 3-4 sessions per week is optimal.

questions.label: How many strict pull-ups can you do right now (no kip, no swing, dead hang to chin over bar)?
questions.help: 3-5 minimum. Below that, the muscle-up work is premature and this program will route you to First Strict Pull-Up first.

options.label: 0-2 strict reps
options.hint: Prerequisite gate fires — routes to First Strict Pull-Up

questions.label: How many strict ring dips can you do (support position → full lockout → depth at 90° elbow → lockout)?
questions.help: 3-5 minimum. Below that, ring-dip strength is the bottleneck and this program builds it first.

questions.label: How long can you hold a false-grip dead hang (wrist on top of the ring, no thumb over)?
Have you ever done a strict ring muscle-up?

options.label: Two or more unbroken
options.hint: Program not optimised for you — see Block 2 when it ships

questions.label: Have you had shoulder pain during any overhead pressing, dip, or hanging work in the last 12 months?
Any elbow tendon pain (medial or lateral) currently or in the last 3 months?
questions.help: The ring dip support position loads medial elbow. If current, we defer ring dip work and use band-assisted dip only.

questions.label: Do you have an acute shoulder injury (rotator cuff tear, labral tear, dislocation) in the last 6 months?
I understand this program is a training template and not medical advice. I'll stop and see a clinician if shoulder or elbow pain persists after a session.

physical_tests.label: Strict pull-up — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: Warm up shoulders 3 minutes. Dead hang start, chin clearly over the bar, controlled descent to full hang. No kip. Record clean reps. Must be ≥ 3 to unlock Tier B.

physical_tests.label: Strict ring dip — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: Rings at chest height. Support position → lower to 90° elbow → lock out. Full range, no leg swing. Record clean reps. Must be ≥ 3 to unlock Tier B.

physical_tests.label: False-grip dead hang — max seconds
physical_tests.instructions: Set rings at hanging height. Grip with wrist on top of the ring (fingers curled around the strap). Hang until grip fails. Record seconds. Zero counts.

physical_tests.label: False-grip strict pull-up — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: From false-grip hang, pull chest to rings. Reset false grip on every rep if it slips. Record clean reps.

physical_tests.label: Ring support hold (locked out) — max seconds
physical_tests.instructions: Muscle up into support (or step up from a box). Hold rings straight-arm turned out, hollow body. Record seconds until form breaks.

consent.label: I understand this is a training template, not medical advice. I'll consult a clinician for shoulder or elbow pain that persists past a session.
I agree to stop the session if shoulder pain appears during a hang, transition, or support hold — no training through it.

safety_gates.block_title: Wait for the acute injury to resolve
safety_gates.block_body: An acute shoulder injury needs healing time and clinical assessment. Come back once you're cleared to load the shoulder in the ring support position.

The strict muscle-up is a strength move stitched from a false-grip pull-up, a transition, and a ring dip. Under 3 strict pull-ups, the transition drills groove a compensation. Run First Strict Pull-Up first and return here at 3+ strict reps.

Under 3 strict ring dips, the top-half of the muscle-up will collapse. The Tier A phase of this program is a ring-dip build — it's a legitimate use of your time here — but you may prefer to run a dedicated dip program first. If you continue, the Tier A phase becomes your ring-dip build.

plan_tiers.label: Tier A — Prerequisites met, ring dips + false grip building
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 3-5 strict ring dips, 15-second false-grip hang, first false-grip ring rows.

program_adjustments.note: Prep tier — ring dip build + false grip tolerance dominate. Transition drills locked out until Tier B unlocks.

plan_tiers.label: Tier B — Transition drills unlocked
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 10-12: seated-band transition mastered, low-ring transition mastered, first jump-assisted muscle-up.

program_adjustments.note: Reference tier. Seated-band transition weeks 1-3, low-ring transition weeks 3-6, jump-assist muscle-up weeks 5-8, first strict attempt from week 8.

plan_tiers.label: Tier C — First strict rep hunt
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 2-3 strict ring muscle-ups unbroken, or 1 reliable + reduced set-up time.

program_adjustments.note: Consolidation. First strict rep tested weekly. Volume via low-ring reps + weighted dip / weighted false-grip pull-up (+2.5 kg) from week 4.

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — Ring dip base + false-grip tolerance (Tier A)
phases.goal: Build 3-5 strict ring dips + 15-second false-grip hang. No transition drills yet.
phases.template_note: Blocked practice weeks 1-2, interleaved weeks 3+. Ring dip support hold + negative → full dip is the Tier A backbone.
notes: The support hold isolates the lockout — the exact position the muscle-up finishes in.
False-grip work capped at 3 minutes accumulated per session for weeks 1-2 (engineering choice; the wrist tissue tolerance is analogous to handstand wrist prep — Wiesinger 2019 mechanism basis).

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — Transition mechanics (Tier B)
phases.goal: Groove the transition mechanic. Seated-band → low-ring → jump-assisted → first strict attempt week 8.
phases.template_note: Weeks 1-2 blocked (each session focuses on one link of the chain), weeks 3+ interleaved. Transition negatives from support are the highest-transfer drill.
notes: Video review after every low-ring or jump-assist attempt as an optional self-controlled feedback (Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002).
First strict attempt is a cold, first-movement-of-session test — not the finisher.

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — First rep consolidation (Tier C)
phases.goal: 1 rep → 2-3 unbroken. Weighted preview from week 4.
phases.template_note: Fully interleaved. Volume via low-ring reps + weighted dip / weighted false-grip pull-up. Weekly max-rep retest.
notes: Weighted preview: +2.5 kg dip or +2.5 kg false-grip pull-up from week 4 IF strict muscle-up count ≥ 1.

blocks.name: Shoulder + wrist prep — every session
blocks.note: Band pull-aparts + scap CARs + wrist prep. Non-optional in weeks 1-3.

blocks.name: Ring dip ladder
blocks.note: Support hold → negative → full dip → deep dip. The top half of the muscle-up. Tier A primary.

blocks.name: False-grip ladder (Tier A/B)
blocks.note: False-grip hang → false-grip ring row → false-grip pull-up. Wrist adaptation to the on-top-of-ring position is the bottleneck.

blocks.name: False-grip pull-up sets (Tier B/C)
blocks.note: False-grip strict pull-ups as the pull half of the muscle-up. Weighted from Tier C week 4 if capability allows.

blocks.name: Transition drills (Tier B/C)
blocks.note: The bottleneck. Seated-band → low-ring negative → low-ring positive. Negatives from support are the highest-transfer drill (Roig 2009 eccentric-heavy meta).

blocks.name: Low-ring muscle-up practice (Tier B/C)
blocks.note: Rings set so feet touch ground. Full muscle-up mechanic without the full load. Progression: assisted with feet → jump-assist → strict low-ring → attempt strict full-ring.

items.note: First strict rep test — cold, first movement in the session.

blocks.name: Strict pull-up sub-max sets (Tier B/C)
blocks.note: Maintain the strict pull-up base while training the muscle-up. Doubles / triples at 60-70% max.

blocks.name: Pull-up maintenance (Tier A)
blocks.note: Hold the strict pull-up count while Tier A builds the dip. Two sub-max sets, no failure.

blocks.name: Active hollow + straight-arm shoulder integrity
blocks.note: Hollow-body hold + straight-arm pull-down (band) support the muscle-up shape and protect the straight-arm-loaded portions.

weekly_template.note: Multi-dimensional generation: the generator picks 2-3 drills per session at composition time based on the user's capability_profile. This template declares slot layout only.
placement_principles: 48h between the two hardest ring-loaded sessions in the week.
Do not run this program the same day as a heavy overhead press session — same joint system.
First strict muscle-up attempt is always the first movement of the session — cold, well-rested.
If you miss a session, don't double up (Shea 2000 spacing effect).

progression_rules.assessment_note: Judge by next-morning shoulder / elbow / wrist symptom score. Video review of best attempt is optional feedback (self-controlled).

states.label: Hold — engine substitutes lower-load drills for the transition set

conditions.or: life_load 7+ or sleep < 6h two nights running

states.label: Skip today's session or do shoulder prep + hollow only

progression_rules.week_end_rule: If the week's key retest (max muscle-up reps for C, false-grip hang seconds + ring dip reps for A/B) improved or held → advance. If regressed AND symptom scores elevated → hold or drop level.
progression_rules.escalation: Two red days in a week → skip the heavier transition or muscle-up test session. Persistent shoulder or wrist pain > 3 days → stop, see a clinician.

daily_log_schema.derived_state_rule: red if any symptom score > 6 OR new_acute_injury; amber if any 4-6 OR life_load >= 7; else green

immediate_actions.action: Complete the intake questionnaire and 5 physical tests within 3 days of starting.
immediate_actions.reason: The prerequisite gates fire on the pull-up + ring dip counts. Missing values default to the safety-first floor and may route you unnecessarily to prep work.

immediate_actions.action: Set up rings at variable heights — you need both dead-hang height AND low-ring (feet-touch) height across the block.
immediate_actions.reason: Low-ring practice is a Tier B / C primary. Rings only at chest / support height limits the whole progression.

immediate_actions.action: Read the shoulder-pain-stops-session rule and agree to it.
immediate_actions.reason: Ring support and false-grip loading are end-range shoulder positions. Pain-through reinforces compensation.

immediate_actions.action: Set up a phone stand — video review is the highest-value feedback for the transition mechanic.
immediate_actions.reason: Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002: self-controlled feedback outperforms forced schedules. The video review button only works if a clip exists.

physiological_targets: False-grip tolerance — the wrist position (radial-flexed with hand on top of ring) loads flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi radialis in a novel pattern. Vidal-Rovira 2024 (small-sample) documents higher forearm activation vs standard hang. Tendon adaptation timeframe is Wiesinger 2019 analog (~8-12 weeks for early collagen turnover) — flagged as engineering choice on exact volume.

Transition mechanic — the muscle-up transition is a straight-arm-to-bent-arm shift with elbows travelling from behind to in front of the body at chest height. No RCT-derived dose-response. Roig 2009 eccentric-heavy meta supports the negatives-from-support drill as the highest-transfer analog.

Ring dip strength — the top half of the muscle-up. Ring dips load rotator cuff + long head of biceps at end range more than parallel bar dips (Dickie 2017, Youdas 2010 dip variant EMG). Support hold isolates the lockout — the exact position the muscle-up finishes in.

Straight-arm shoulder integrity — support lockout and straight-arm pull-down train the shoulder in end-range flexion and extension. Sadowski 2021 (straight-arm press to handstand: 3× BW shoulder moment) is the closest analog for peak load; support lockout under bodyweight is lower but still significant.

Motor learning stages — Fitts & Posner 1967 cognitive → associative → autonomous. Tier A/B is cognitive → early associative for the transition. Blocked practice weeks 1-2 (Wulf & Shea 2002 complex-skill caveat), interleaved from week 3.

External-focus cues — Wulf 1998, 2013 (15-year review, ~100 studies). Halperin 2019: external focus specifically improves 1RM strength / force / velocity in weightlifting. Cues target the ring path (rings to sternum, drive rings down past hips), not the muscles.

session_rationale.block_shoulder_prep: Band pull-aparts + scap CARs + wrist prep. Kibler 2013 scapular dyskinesis + Reinold 2007 supraspinatus EMG data support the pre-session activation dose. Non-optional in weeks 1-3 while wrist and shoulder are novel-load-tolerant.
session_rationale.block_ring_dip_ladder: Support hold → negative → full dip → deep dip. The top half of the muscle-up. Youdas 2010 (dip variants EMG) informs the ladder — deep dip biases the anterior deltoid + serratus recruitment that the muscle-up finish demands.
session_rationale.block_false_grip_ladder: False-grip hang → false-grip ring row → false-grip pull-up. Wrist adaptation to the on-top-of-ring position is the bottleneck. Vidal-Rovira 2024 forearm EMG data supports the false-grip-as-separate-capability framing.
session_rationale.block_false_grip_pullup: False-grip strict pull-ups as the pull half of the muscle-up. Grip must survive the concentric — a strict pull-up in standard grip does not transfer directly. Trained as its own capability.
session_rationale.block_transition_progression: The bottleneck. Seated-band → low-ring negative → low-ring positive. Negatives from support are the highest-transfer drill for the elbow-travel mechanic. Roig 2009 eccentric-heavy meta: eccentric training produces greater strength gains than concentric-only for matched work.
session_rationale.block_low_ring_practice: Rings set so feet touch ground. Full muscle-up mechanic without the full load. Chained progression: assisted with feet → jump-assist → strict low-ring → attempt strict full-ring. Variability of practice (Schmidt 1975 schema theory) as the progression accumulates.
session_rationale.block_pullup_sets_submax: Maintain the strict pull-up base while training the muscle-up. Doubles/triples at 60-70% max — non-failure volume, Zourdos 2019 velocity-loss threshold literature supports staying well shy of RIR 0.
session_rationale.block_pullup_maintenance: Tier A only — hold the strict pull-up count while dip and false grip build. Two sub-max sets, no failure. Coyle 1984 detraining-timecourse analog: maintenance dose preserves the capability without competing with the primary training focus.
session_rationale.block_active_hollow: Hollow-body hold + straight-arm pull-down (band). The muscle-up shape is a hollow shape at the pull; the support lockout is a straight-arm loaded position. Reinforce both with low-cost isometric and band work. McGill 2015 core-endurance work supports the isometric hollow dose.

evidence_base.progression_rationale: Weeks 1-2 are blocked practice per Wulf & Shea 2002 (crucial caveat: CI benefits from simple lab skills often reverse in complex real-world skills). From week 3 the multi-dimensional generator interleaves 2-3 drills per session across the user's weakest capabilities (Henry 1968, Proteau 1992 specificity). Tier assignment at intake seeds capability_profile.estimated_level per capability_domain. Transition drills are gated: the seated-band transition requires mu_transition_control_level ≥ 1, low-ring negative requires ≥ 2, low-ring positive requires ≥ 3, first strict attempt from week 6-8 requires the full chain. Weekly max-rep retest (Tier C) or weekly false-grip-hang / ring-dip retest (Tier A/B). Full re-assessment at 4 and 8 weeks re-seeds the capability_profile.
evidence_base.outcome_evidence: No cohort ETAs — Ackerman 1988 (early-stage cognitive ability correlates), Wu 2014 (3× variance in visuomotor rotation learning). Realistic 8-week block outcomes: Tier A — 3-5 strict ring dips, 15-second false-grip hang, first false-grip ring rows. Tier B — first low-ring muscle-up, first jump-assist, first strict attempt at week 8. Tier C — 2-3 strict ring muscle-ups unbroken. Direct RCT for a strict-muscle-up protocol is nonexistent; the drill order is derived from analog literature (Roig 2009 eccentric; Youdas 2010 dip EMG; Reinold 2007 rotator-cuff load; Kibler 2013 scapular dyskinesis; Wulf 1998/2013 motor learning; Shea 1979 CI; Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002 self-controlled feedback) and coach-consensus (Sommer 2008 GymnasticBodies commentary; Low 2016 Overcoming Gravity commentary — cited as coach references, not evidence). Individual variation on the transition is large: some athletes crack it in weeks, others take a full year even with adequate prerequisite strength.

tier_c_first_rep.weighted_preview: +2.5 kg dip or +2.5 kg false-grip pull-up

contraindications: Shoulder pain during a hang, transition, or support hold — session ends immediately. Do not train through it. Reinold 2007 supraspinatus load data + Sadowski 2021 straight-arm shoulder moment analog support the caution.
Acute rotator-cuff injury, labral tear, or shoulder dislocation in the last 6 months — dead hangs, ring support, and transition attempts contraindicated until cleared.
Currently symptomatic medial or lateral elbow tendinopathy — defer ring dip work and transition negatives. Use scap and hollow work only until cleared.
Acute wrist injury (TFCC tear, ligament instability) in the last 6 weeks — false-grip work is prohibited; hollow + hang-only substitutes.
Persistent cervical radiculopathy — avoid dead hangs and false-grip hangs entirely; the traction can inflame nerve root symptoms.
Uncontrolled hypertension with Valsalva concern — the transition and support hold provoke Valsalva. Use exhale-on-effort breathing or defer until controlled.
evidence_base.adaptive_engine_hooks: Shoulder + elbow + wrist symptom scores are the primary daily signals. Any > 6 for a day → gate the next session to shoulder prep + hollow only. Any 4-6 → engine proposes swapping the heaviest transition or ring drill for a lower-level substitute (proposal, user Accepts). Weekly max-rep retest: two consecutive weeks with a regression AND symptom score up → engine drops the user's mu_transition_control level by 1 and re-composes with lower-level drills next week. Video review self-select frequency is tracked (motivation proxy per Chiviacowsky & Wulf) but doesn't gate anything. Weighted preview from Tier C week 4 unlocks IF strict muscle-up count ≥ 1 (engine-gated). All engine adjustments respect the confirm-first rule.
engineering_choices_flagged: 3-5 strict pull-up + 3-5 ring dip prerequisite gate — coach consensus (Sommer 2008, Low 2016 coach commentary), not RCT-derived.
False grip volume cap (3 min accumulated in weeks 1-2) — Wiesinger 2019 tendon-adaptation mechanism basis, no direct dose-response.
Seated-band → low-ring → jump-assist → strict progression — coach convention, not empirically tested.
Weekly max-rep retest cadence — engineering choice; matches multi-dimensional retest cadence used in Handstand Walk and First Strict Pull-Up.
First strict rep attempt from week 6-8 in Tier B — pragmatic; earlier attempts often fail without the transition groove, later leaves upside on the table.
Weighted preview (+2.5 kg) at Tier C — coach convention.
Ring dip support hold as Tier A entry drill — pragmatic; lockout position isolates the muscle-up finish position, but exact hold-time doses (15s, 30s, etc.) are engineering choice.
3-4 sessions/week — daily-short-beats-long inference from Karni 1998 + Walker 2003 + Shea 2000. No direct muscle-up-frequency RCT.

references.authors: Roig M, O'Brien K, Kirk G, et al.
references.title: The effects of eccentric versus concentric resistance training on muscle strength and mass in healthy adults: a systematic review with meta-analysis
references.used_for: Eccentric training produces greater strength gains than concentric-only. Anchors the transition-negative-from-support drill as the highest-transfer analog for the muscle-up transition.

references.authors: Youdas JW, Amundson CL, Cicirello KS, Hellmers CJ, Hollman JH
references.title: Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise
references.source: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(12):3404-3414
references.used_for: Pull-variant EMG hierarchy. Supports the false-grip-as-separate-capability framing and the grip-position-matters logic. Referenced by the shared drill library.

references.authors: Reinold MM, Wilk KE, Fleisig GS, et al.
references.title: Electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises
references.source: Journal of Orthopaedic and Sports Physical Therapy 37(9):519-527
references.used_for: Supraspinatus EMG data — informs the shoulder-pain-stops-session rule and the pre-session prep dose.

references.authors: Kibler WB, Ludewig PM, McClure PW, Michener LA, Bak K, Sciascia AD
references.title: Clinical implications of scapular dyskinesis in shoulder injury: the 2013 consensus statement
references.used_for: Scapular dyskinesis pattern in overhead / hang loading. Anchors the shoulder-prep-before-every-session rule.

references.authors: Sadowski J, et al.
references.title: Kinematic and kinetic analysis of the straight-arm press to handstand
references.used_for: 3× bodyweight shoulder moment during straight-arm press to handstand — the closest analog for ring support end-range shoulder load.

references.authors: Wulf G, Höß M, Prinz W
references.title: Instructions for motor learning: differential effects of internal versus external focus of attention
references.used_for: External focus vs internal focus foundation. Anchors the external-focus cue on every drill card.

references.authors: Wulf G
references.title: Attentional focus and motor learning: a review of 15 years
references.source: International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology 6(1):77-104
references.used_for: 15-year review supporting the external-focus default.

references.authors: Wulf G, Shea CH
references.title: Principles derived from the study of simple skills do not generalize to complex skill learning
references.used_for: Crucial caveat: CI benefit is smaller for complex skills. Anchors phase-gated CI schedule (blocked 1-2, interleaved 3+).

references.authors: Shea JB, Morgan RL
references.title: Contextual interference effects on the acquisition, retention, and transfer of a motor skill
references.source: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory 5(2):179-187
references.used_for: Foundational CI study. Blocked practice benefits acquisition, random benefits retention.

references.authors: Karni A, Meyer G, Rey-Hipolito C, et al.
references.title: The acquisition of skilled motor performance: fast and slow experience-driven changes in primary motor cortex
references.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 95(3):861-868
references.used_for: Fast (within-session) and slow (across-session) learning phases. Anchors daily-short-beats-long.

references.authors: Walker MP, Brakefield T, Hobson JA, Stickgold R
references.title: Dissociable stages of human memory consolidation and reconsolidation
references.used_for: Dissociable consolidation stages. Supports daily short skill exposure.

references.authors: Shea CH, Lai Q, Black C, Park JH
references.title: Spacing practice sessions across days benefits the learning of motor skills
references.used_for: Spacing effect: spread practice across days beats massed practice. Anchors multi-session weekly template.

references.authors: Henry FM
references.title: Specificity vs. generality in learning motor skill
references.used_for: Specificity hypothesis. Anchors per-capability drill selection. Also justifies the deliberate separation of strict vs kipping muscle-up.

references.authors: Proteau L, Marteniuk RG, Lévesque L
references.title: A sensorimotor basis for motor learning: evidence indicating specificity of practice
references.used_for: Learning is specific to sensory conditions of practice. Supports multi-dimensional per-capability approach.

references.title: Constraints on the development of coordination

references.title: Self-controlled feedback: does it enhance learning because performers get feedback when they need it?

references.used_for: Skill-readiness assessment and prerequisite gating as injury-mitigation heuristic. Anchors the strict-pull-up + ring-dip prerequisite gate.

references.authors: Schmidt RA
references.title: A schema theory of discrete motor skill learning
references.used_for: Schema theory: variability of practice builds recall and recognition schemas. Anchors the low-ring / jump-assist / strict variety.

references.authors: Sinnett AM, Cheatham SW, Brismée JM
references.title: The effect of band-assisted pull-up training on muscular strength and pull-up performance
references.source: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research (or proceedings) — verification pending
references.used_for: Band-assisted EMG is lower than strict — reinforces the framing that band assistance is a groove drill, not a strength driver. Applies to any band-assisted work referenced in this program.

references.used_for: Higher forearm activation in false-grip vs standard. Small sample, flagged for founder science-advisor review. Supports the false-grip-as-separate-capability framing but is not the load-bearing citation.

references.authors: Dickie JA, Faulkner JA, Barnes MJ, Lark SD
references.title: Electromyographic analysis of muscle activation during pull-up variations
references.used_for: EMG data on pull-up variants — supports the drill-library ordering and the false-grip pull-up as its own capability.

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale

onboarding_steps.title: Prerequisite check + false-grip test
onboarding_steps.body_md: Muscle-Up assumes 3 strict pull-ups and 3 strict ring dips. Below either, the plan routes you to prep work first. False-grip hang is your entry test for the pull half of the muscle-up.

onboarding_steps.title: How Muscle-Up Acquisition works
onboarding_steps.body_md: Three to four short sessions a week. False-grip work, ring dip ladder, and — from Tier B — the transition drills that are the actual bottleneck. Kipping muscle-ups are a different skill; this program stays strict. If shoulders, elbows, or wrists complain, we back off — no exceptions.
